visuals.concept: CG position relative to centre of lift/pressure determines longitudinal stability

source.notes: Positive stability figure; text states centre of lift behind centre of gravity with a balancing downward tail force.

brief.student_must_understand: Longitudinal stability depends on the CG position relative to the centre of lift/pressure, with the tail providing a balancing downforce in the stable arrangement.
preserve: Original lift, weight and tail-force vectors
Relative fore-aft position shown in the handbook

Make the CG/lift relationship easy to scan

source.notes: Typical airplane drag curves showing induced drag, parasite drag and total drag.

brief.student_must_understand: The parasite/profile-drag curve rises with speed while induced drag falls; total drag is the sum and reaches a minimum at Vmd.
refine: Emphasize the parasite-drag relationship without obscuring the source

visuals.mapping_reason: Question 1153 tests recognition of the parasite/profile-drag curve; the visual clearly labels parasite drag and shows why it rises with speed relative to induced and total drag.

visuals.concept: Dihedral improves lateral stability in the rolling plane

source.notes: Effect of dihedral figure showing the upward wing angle and handbook text explaining its restoring roll tendency during a sideslip.

brief.student_must_understand: Dihedral is the upward angle of the wings from root to tip and is used to improve lateral/roll stability.
refine: Explain the restoring roll sequence after a disturbance

visuals.mapping_reason: Question 1168 asks what stability dihedral improves; the visual identifies lateral/roll stability and explains the restoring tendency that creates it.

visuals.concept: Higher lift-to-drag ratio produces a shallower glide angle

source.notes: Forces in a glide; handbook text states that reducing drag makes the glide angle smaller and L/D measures gliding efficiency.

brief.student_must_understand: A high L/D ratio means more forward distance for each unit of height lost, producing a shallow glide.
preserve: Original lift, drag, weight and resultant vectors
refine: Contrast the shallow and steeper glide examples

visuals.mapping_reason: Question 1239 asks what glide angle results from a high L/D ratio; the visual directly contrasts higher-L/D shallow glide with lower-L/D steeper glide.
